class_summary.overall: The class has partial understanding of Fourier Transform.
observations: Some students know it is related to frequency.
Several students think it is just a formula.
Some students do not understand why the concept matters.

teacher_recommendation.headline: Do not restart with the formula.
recommended_flow: Start with a curiosity hook: Why can a song, an image, and a quantum wave all be understood through frequencies?
Use a prism analogy: a prism splits white light into colors, and Fourier Transform splits a complex signal into frequencies.
Show a visual explanation: complex waveform -> Fourier Transform prism -> simple sine waves.
Then introduce the formal definition: time domain shows how the signal changes over time, while frequency domain shows what frequencies build the signal.
Finish with a micro-quiz to test understanding.

differentiated_materials.title: Level 1: Confused Students
differentiated_materials.explanation: Imagine listening to a song. It sounds like one complex sound, but inside it there are many notes and frequencies mixed together. Fourier Transform helps us separate the sound and see what frequencies are inside.
differentiated_materials.analogy: Fourier Transform is like a prism. A prism splits white light into colors. Fourier Transform splits a complex signal into frequencies.
differentiated_materials.task: Explain Fourier Transform using the prism analogy.

differentiated_materials.title: Level 2: Partially Understood Students
differentiated_materials.explanation: In the time domain, we see how a signal changes over time. In the frequency domain, we see what frequencies make up the signal. Fourier Transform is the bridge between these two views.
differentiated_materials.analogy: It is like changing camera angles: one view shows motion over time, and the other view shows the hidden ingredients of the signal.
differentiated_materials.task: Draw a simple diagram showing time domain on the left, Fourier Transform in the middle, and frequency domain on the right.

differentiated_materials.title: Level 3: Ready to Apply Students
differentiated_materials.explanation: Frequency representation is useful when the hidden structure of a signal matters more than its raw shape over time.
differentiated_materials.analogy: It is like reading the ingredients list of a complex recipe instead of only looking at the finished dish.
differentiated_materials.task: Choose one application of Fourier Transform: music, MRI, image compression, or quantum mechanics. Explain why frequency representation is useful in that field.

visual_aid.prompt: Create a clean educational diagram showing a complex waveform on the left passing through a glowing prism labeled Fourier Transform, then splitting into several simple sine waves on the right.

micro_quiz: If a song is made of many notes mixed together, what does Fourier Transform help us see?
Why is Fourier Transform like a prism?
What is the difference between time domain and frequency domain?
Trap question: Is Fourier Transform only a formula? Explain why or why not.
current_lesson_plan: Introduce the definition of Fourier Transform.
Explain time domain and frequency domain.
